maria: FYI onboarding mosaic-xlite-v1 hit a bunch of weird conversion interactions, posting quick notes.
ashwin: what symptoms are you seeing? kv head errors or tokenization drift?
maria: both. quantized q4f16 build + HF config -> redwood conversion. After conversion for some runs we get KV SHAPE MISMATCH on serve, and eval shows e2e perf drop on long prompts.
kate: any stack traces or logs? can you paste the exact error?
maria: here, from the conversion smoke-run:
```
ERROR: KV SHAPE MISMATCH: expected num_key_value_heads=16, got 8 for layer 12
Model config: {"num_key_value_heads":16,"rope_scaling":{"type":"linear","factor":0.5},"max_position_embeddings":2048,"sliding_window":512}
Conversion output header: num_kv_heads=8, kv_stride=2
```
sam: interesting. conversion output having kv_stride=2 suggests our HF config parser might be halving heads when quant grouping is enabled.
ashwin: is quantization step changing tensor layout? pack_group_size could affect how we map kv heads if we assume contiguous head blocks.
kate: also saw rope_scaling in this model set to 0.5. we've historically applied rope rescale on the runtime side; double-applying it during conversion could shift rotary positions and, with sliding_window, cause token index misalignment.
maria: yes. reproducer script: `tools/hf2redwood/repro_kv_check.py --model mosaic-xlite-v1 --check-ropescale --check-kv` produced the above and a tokenizer mismatch report.
eval-bot: automated eval: embed_cosine_drop=0.07, perplexity_increase=+1.8 on long-context dataset (>1500 tokens). Baseline was stable pre-quant.
ashwin: could be two things stacked: (1) tokenization/special token mapping causing off-by-one so sliding_window slices tokens differently; (2) conversion's num_kv mapping logic misreads HF config when rope_scaling present.
sam: quick triage idea: run conversion with `--force-num-kv 16 --preserve-rope-scaling` and diff param headers. If shapes align, we know conversion decided incorrectly.
maria: tried forcing num-kv, shapes OK, but eval still has a small delta. when I toggled rope rescale at runtime off, metrics returned to baseline.
kate: that points to double-rescale. Maybe the HF config carries a rope_scaling hint and our converter applies it into the serialized RoPE coeffs, and runtime also applies rescale when a non-default rope tag exists.
ashwin: agree. two fixes: a) make converter write a `converted_meta.json` with rope_applied: true/false and num_kv_override flag; b) runtime to refuse double-apply and log a warning.
infra-bot: deploy queued: patch branch `fix/conv-rope-kvmeta` created, CI lint passing.
maria: I'll attach the minimal reproducer and sample config in the ticket. also note tokenizer special token mapping: HF had `bos_token` set to `<s>`, converter mapped to `<|start|>` which shifted chat template indices when sliding_window boundary hit.
sam: Oof. Chat templates + sliding_window boundaries are brittle. We should add a unit test: long prompt roundtrip where `chat_template` + `sliding_window` preserves special token positions.
kate: Agreed. I'll add an eval in the onboarding pipeline: 2 long-context prompts, compare token offsets and kv cache snapshots at layer 0.
maria: one more datapoint: quantization pack_group_size=64 produced slightly different per-head scales, might expose an indexing assumption in our `kv_head_remap` routine.
ashwin: OK. Action items: 1) maria attach reproducer + configs to ticket 3872; 2) kate add long-context chat_template unit test; 3) sam add converter guard to emit explicit meta and CLI flag `--preserve-rope-scaling`; 4) infra: land branch, run dedicated ci on quantized artifacts. I'll file PRs.
maria: thanks — will post PR links and logs. tagging @kate @sam for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
